title: 1987 Constitution, Article VIII, Section 1
text: This course-authored fixture summary states that Philippine judicial power includes settling actual controversies involving enforceable rights. It also includes deciding whether a government branch or instrumentality committed grave abuse of discretion amounting to lack or excess of jurisdiction.

title: 1997 Rules of Civil Procedure, Rule 65
citation: RULES OF COURT, Rule 65, secs. 1 and 4
text: This course-authored fixture summary states that certiorari addresses judicial or quasi-judicial action taken without jurisdiction, beyond jurisdiction, or with grave abuse of discretion. The petitioner must lack an appeal or another plain, speedy, and adequate remedy in the ordinary course of law. The petition ordinarily must be filed within sixty days from notice of the challenged judgment, order, or resolution.

title: GSIS Board of Trustees v. Court of Appeals-Cebu City
citation: GSIS Board of Trustees v. Court of Appeals-Cebu City, G.R. No. 230953, June 20, 2018
text: This course-authored fixture summary describes certiorari as an independent action available only when no appeal or other plain, speedy, and adequate remedy exists. It states the general rule that certiorari cannot replace a lost appeal and characterizes grave abuse as patent and gross. It also notes that a party relying on an exception must substantiate the reason for departing from the general rule.

title: Punongbayan-Visitacion v. People
citation: Punongbayan-Visitacion v. People, G.R. No. 194214, January 10, 2018
text: This course-authored fixture summary states that appeal and certiorari are generally not interchangeable. On the case's particular facts, the Court treated the certiorari petition as an appeal because it was filed within the appeal period and substantial justice warranted review.

title: Ortigas and Company Limited Partnership v. Court of Appeals
citation: Ortigas and Company Limited Partnership v. Court of Appeals, G.R. No. 260118, February 12, 2024
text: This course-authored fixture summary explains that certiorari may remain available when ordinary appeal is not a plain, speedy, and adequate remedy. It identifies a properly supported denial-of-due-process claim and broader interests of justice among circumstances requiring careful exception analysis.

title: Unverified bar-review outline
text: An unattributed outline claims that certiorari is always available after an appeal deadline expires.
